blocks.x: Cyber & Zero-Trust applied to Streaming & Digital Platforms. This page sets out the operating context, the delivery pattern we run, the services and platforms involved, and the outcomes we commit to.

Streaming platforms live on two curves: engagement (personalization, discovery, retention) and unit economics (encoding, delivery, churn). Both are decision engines — and both run better on governed telemetry, evaluation-driven ML and cost telemetry.

items: Password sharing and stream-ripping drain ARPU; enforcement blunt.
Recommendations plateau without governance over objectives (engagement vs. Satisfaction).

blocks.x: The pattern composes AI Security & Model Protection, AI Security & Model Protection, Cyber Resilience & Incident Recovery from the Cybersecurity & Zero-Trust tower, wired into the unit's workflows (Personalization/discovery, Subscriber lifecycle, Delivery cost management) on Dataq Sentinel and Dataq Compass. Governance inherits the sector frame — Privacy/consent among others — with evidence generated by the delivery itself.

items: Secure at the control plane: posture, workload and data security engineered into the platform.
Secure the models themselves: prompt-injection defense, agent containment and AI red-teaming.
Assume breach, plan recovery: resilience engineered, rehearsed and measured.
Sharing analytics with tiered enforcement (ARPU protected)

blocks.x: At industry level, the same pattern

At Telecom, Media & Entertainment level this capability reads as: identity-centric access and segmentation across core functions (lateral movement eliminated in validation). The sub-industry page narrows it to the unit's workflows, regimes and KPIs.

The engagement cadence below is the standard pattern for this capability. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
